- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >65.00), model often overshoots and fails to revert; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% and add slight downward slope to reflect mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.30), model underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon; shift forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for first 5–7 days, especially if sentiment is weakly positive.  
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > +0.30), model often overestimates upside; cap forecast at +2–3% above recent high or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral.  
- Model exhibits lag in reacting to sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days, adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect new trend.
